rich_summary: Vasudeva recounts to Yudhishthira the origins of Parashurama (Rama of Bhrigu’s line) and the destruction of the Kshatriya warrior class. Through a mistaken exchange of sanctified food prepared by the sage Richika, destinies are reversed: Satyavati bears Jamadagni, a tranquil Brahmana, while her lineage produces the fiery forces that lead to Parashurama’s birth. Jamadagni’s son Rama gains divine weapons from Shiva and eventually kills the thousand‑armed king Kartavirya Arjuna after the king’s sons murder Jamadagni. Enraged, Rama repeatedly exterminates Kshatriyas across the earth. After giving the conquered world to the sage Kasyapa, surviving Kshatriya children hidden among common people are restored as rulers. The tale explains both Parashurama’s legendary wrath and the later re‑emergence of Kshatriya lineages.

highlight_spans.why: Opening frame where Vaisampayana introduces Vasudeva’s explanation of how the earth became filled with Kshatriyas.
Richika explains the destinies tied to the sanctified food—one producing a fierce Kshatriya destroyer and the other a tranquil Brahmana—setting up the central twist.
Introduction of Rama (Parashurama), blazing like fire and destined to become the exterminator of the Kshatriyas.
The murder of Jamadagni by the sons of Arjuna—an emotional turning point that triggers Rama’s terrible vengeance.
Description of Rama slaughtering Kshatriyas repeatedly until the earth is emptied of them, emphasizing the scale of the destruction.
The Earth goddess reveals hidden Kshatriya heirs who will repopulate the warrior class, explaining the survival of royal lineages.

top_scenes.scene_text: Parashurama, blazing with fury and wielding Shiva’s radiant axe, cuts down the thousand‑armed king Kartavirya Arjuna on a battlefield.
The sage Richika prepares two bowls of sanctified milk‑and‑rice while Satyavati and her mother unknowingly exchange them, altering destiny.
The Earth goddess appeals to the sage Kasyapa, revealing hidden young Kshatriya princes raised among animals, artisans, and forests.
